reviewed_by: Blind judgment Reviewer (subagent, 0 tool uses, samples inline), batch fix-loop-tick-2 2026-08-20

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both halves of the competency are directly addressed. Lines: seed 42 'How is a straight line different from a curved line?', seed 46 'Why is the edge of a ruler called a straight line?', seed 45 'The path of a winding river bends smoothly and changes direction.' Surfaces: seed 44 'How is a flat surface different from a curved surface?', seed 43 (box, 'six faces that are each flat'), seed 604 'What kind of surface does the cover of a closed book have?'. Nothing asks for area, perimeter, or face/edge/vertex counting.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Identification sub-cases are balanced at three keyed appearances each (straight line 42/46/500, curved line 42/45/501, flat surface 43/44/604, curved surface 44/502/603). The 'explain' verb is the gap: only seeds 42, 44 and 46 explain, and 42 and 44 are the same item with 'line' swapped for 'surface', sharing the distractor frame 'Both of them bend in the same way.' No item asks the pupil to explain a surface property of a named 3-dimensional object, though the competency reads 'flat and curved surfaces OF 3-dimensional objects'.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stems are one or two short sentences with concrete physical predicates ('never bends', 'bends all the way around', 'has no bumps or curves'). Contexts are everyday Grade 2 objects: ruler, box, ball, book, river. 'solid figure' (seed 603) is glossed in-item with 'like a ball'. No multi-step reasoning and no numerical load.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five stem shapes exist (paired contrast, property-clue plus open classification, property-clue plus category-constrained classification, justification, bare classification), so there is no single-template collapse. The variety fails at the option level: seven of ten items (43, 45, 500, 501, 502, 603, 604) present the identical four-item menu straight line / curved line / flat surface / curved surface, merely permuted, and the two explanation items recycle one distractor kit.

competency_alignment.rationale: Nothing exceeds scope; no face/edge/vertex counting, symmetry, area or solid names. Seed 43 uses 'faces' but defines it in place ('six faces that are each flat'). Recorded reading: if 'of 3-dimensional objects' is taken to govern both halves, seeds 45 (a river) and 501 (a circle) anchor lines to non-3-D referents; under the natural reading the phrase attaches to the surfaces clause and these are in scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The only quantity in the set is 'six faces' (seed 43), correct for a box and within Grade 2 counting range. All contexts are physically accurate: a ruler's edge does not bend, a ball's surface curves in every direction, a closed book's cover is flat.

problems_reported: Duplicate item, seeds 502 and 603: both are ball/curved-surface classification with the same clue predicate; seed 603 names the ball, so its ostensible generalisation to 'solid figure' is not exercised.
Repeated context, seeds 46 and 500: both hang on 'the edge of a ruler never bends', consuming two of five line items while no line item is drawn from the edge of a solid.
Template twins, seeds 42 and 44: identical stem frame and distractor kit with one word substituted, including the verbatim shared distractor 'Both of them bend in the same way.'

Non-functioning distractors, seeds 43/502/603/604: the stem 'What kind of surface ...' grammatically excludes 'straight line' and 'curved line', so a pupil who knows only that a line is not a surface guesses at 50%. Seeds 45/500/501 use the correct 'Which best describes it?' frame that leaves all four options live.
Answer telegraphed in stem, seed 43: 'six faces that are each FLAT' supplies the keyword verbatim for key 'flat surface'. Seed 604 is the well-built version of the same content.

Imprecise referent, seed 501: 'The rim of a circle' -- a circle has no rim; the circle IS the curved line. The key survives both readings so the item is answerable, but the phrasing models sloppy geometry language.
Checked and clean: no wrong or ambiguous keys; no distractor is also true of its key; no mathematically false statement in any stem or key.
